metadata.architecture: eight-channel attention-only residual model with sinusoidal positions, non-affine RMS normalization, and tied readout
metadata.mechanism_hypothesis: Reducing the residual width from 16 to 8 should preserve the attention-based alignment mechanism while removing channels not required to maintain the current public eligibility floor.
metadata.research_alternative_explanation: The 16-channel residual stream may be necessary to represent token identity, position, and carry-relevant attention features simultaneously.
metadata.research_challenged_assumption: The current direction treats a 16-channel residual stream as necessary for eligibility without decisive positive public evidence.
metadata.research_current_explanation: The zero public score does not demonstrate that all 16 residual channels contribute useful digit-alignment or carry information.
metadata.research_decision_rule: Retain only if the graph is valid, remains eligible under the frozen public rule, and reduces trusted parameter count.
metadata.research_discriminating_evidence: Preserved eligibility at lower parameter count favors a low-rank representation; an eligibility decrease favors a minimum-width requirement above eight channels.
metadata.research_evidence: The current 16-channel model has 1264 parameters and a public score of 0.000000, providing no observed accuracy benefit for its full width.
metadata.research_expected_result: The eight-channel model should match the current eligibility outcome with substantially fewer attention and embedding parameters.
metadata.research_next_experiment: Halve every hidden representation from 16 to 8 while preserving the two-head causal-attention topology and all parameter-free mechanisms.
metadata.research_previous_interpretation: Replacing affine layer normalization with non-affine RMS normalization yielded the current 1264-parameter model, which still has a public score of 0.000000.
